text:
support_jamie: FYI CS ping — multiple customers reporting 503s for hosted inference since ~2024-06-21 10:12 UTC. They see upstream worker restarts in the logs.

oncall-bot: alert: hosted-infer-prod: worker_restart_rate exceeded threshold at 10:12 UTC, auto-flagging incidents channel.

eng-aaron: which region/pool is this hitting? any common model or batch pattern?

support_jamie: us-west-2, gpu-pool-12. Customer logs show "inference-runner exited with signal 11" and repeated CUDA OOM messages. CS ticket attached a couple of stack traces.

ashley: customer also saw a flurry of 401 auth errors before the 503 spike — maybe retries caused higher mem pressure?

miguel: pasting the most recent docker log excerpt: ```
[2024-06-21T10:11:59Z] inference-runner[pid=4521]: Allocating KV prefetch buffer size=1,234,560
[2024-06-21T10:12:00Z] inference-runner[pid=4521]: nvml: out of memory trying to allocate 256MB
[2024-06-21T10:12:00Z] inference-runner[pid=4521]: Received signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
[2024-06-21T10:12:01Z] kubelet: container restarted
```

sre_ela: Looks like KV prefetch + large batch/context triggered a GPU allocation spike, then segfault during GPU kernel call. We're seeing the pattern on ~6 nodes in pool-12.

eng-aaron: Can we route live traffic off pool-12 to a fallback variant? Need to reduce customer impact quickly.

product-liz: For high-impact customers we can enable fallback to the cpu_small_model variant — higher latency but avoids GPU OOM. Do we have an automated route?

support_jamie: CS applied manual route overrides for our top 3 affected customers, but smaller customers are still getting 503s.

eng-aaron: Mitigation plan: 1) cordon noisy nodes, 2) set INFER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 and disable KV_PREFETCH on pool-12, 3) enable fallback routing for all bursty requests. Oncall, can you cordon nodes showing repeated SIGSEGV?

oncall-bot: cordon job queued: kubectl label node gpu-node-12a cordoned-by=oncall; job id 84321; timestamp 1717530200.

miguel: additional trace from gdb on one container: ```
#0  0x00007f9c3b2a1c8 in cuMemAlloc (ptr=0x7ffd..., size=268435456) at libcuda.so
#1  0x000055b9a812dabc in allocate_gpu_buffer at gpu_alloc.cpp:134
#2  0x000055b9a80f9d10 in prefetch_kv_cache at kv_prefetch.cpp:78
#3  0x000055b9a8012345 in model_forward at model.cpp:562
```

ashley: Billing system is also seeing a retry storm; billing-robot flagged potential double-charges from client retries. CS asked about credits.

billing-robot: notice: retry_rate spike detected between 10:08-10:18 UTC for pool-12. Preparing credit assessment and opening billing ticket BLG-884.

sre_ela: Temporary workaround in progress: I'm pushing a rolling config to set INFER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 and KV_PREFETCH=off on the daemonset for pool-12. That should reduce peak allocations.

eng-aaron: Command I'm running now: `kubectl set env ds/infer-workers INFER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 KV_PREFETCH=false -n hosted-infer --selector=pool=gpu-pool-12` — rolling update started.

support_jamie: Notifying customers of mitigations and ETA. Will keep them updated.

miguel: I'm collecting dmesg and GPU driver logs and uploading to S3: s3://redwood-debug/upstream-gpu/1717529999/ — includes coredump and nvml logs.

eng-aaron: We need reproducible steps. From logs it looks like requests with huge context (~1.2M tokens) + quantized model trigger large prefetch. Repro idea: send 4 concurrent requests with 1.2M token context and batch_size 4 to LLaMA-XX-quantized.

sre_ela: I'll run an isolated repro on staging with identical worker config and a non-customer workload to confirm. If confirmed, kernel-level handler to guard mem allocs is needed.

product-liz: Also capturing this in the postmortem checklist: 1) routing playbook, 2) billing credits, 3) doc update on max context/kv_prefetch, 4) monitor thresholds.

eng-aaron: Hotfix rolling looks good — early metrics show error rate dropping ~80% in pool-12 and p95 latency down from ~850ms to ~230ms for routed traffic. Will keep monitoring.

oncall-bot: monitor update: hosted-infer-prod pool-12 error-rate decreased at 1717530400; sustained lower error rate for 5m.

support_jamie: CS closed the immediate customer escalations with notes on mitigation and billing follow-up. We'll keep this incident open until postmortem and permanent fix.

eng-aaron: Next steps: collect repro artifacts, run kernel-guard patch in staging, plan rollback of quantized model or add allocation cap in runtime. I'll post follow-up in ~30m.

support_jamie: Thanks everyone. Reopening if anything pops back up.
